label: Original-phase input of 2/n/0/h/w/i/l/u (from step 2 on) in sequences that start with r/3/c/f/d/t
predicate: (phase == 0) & (t >= 2) & isin(in_tok, [tok("2"), tok("n"), tok("0"), tok("h"), tok("w"), tok("i"), tok("l"), tok("u")]) & isin(first_tok, [tok("r"), tok("3"), tok("c"), tok("f"), tok("d"), tok("t")])
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase (98% of mass), never at t=0 or t=1, and peaks at t=3-4. It needs a particular current input (2 is strongest at 7.7x lift, then n, 0, h, w, i, l, u) and an earlier context token from {r,3,c,f,d,t}, most of all a first token r (6x lift). It is stronger on the first occurrence of the input token. The top activations are 2 or n arriving at t=3-5 after r/c/3-heavy prefixes, e.g. c c r r 3 [2]. It is near-silent at the delimiter and in the copy phase. The current-input set alone has 87% recall but 8% precision, and the first-token condition raises precision to only about 0.32, so the neuron depends on a distributed hidden-state combination of tokens that a simple predicate does not fully capture (dev F1 0.42, mass recall 0.70).
